references.text: David also risked his life when he fought against Goliath, a parallel to Jephthah's expression of putting his life at stake
The expression 'to put one's life in one's hand' is also used here to mean risking one's life
Job uses the same expression about taking his life in his hand, which means to risk his life
Describes Jephthah's victory over the Ammonites, whom the Lord gave into his hand, providing background for this confrontation
The context of the conflict with Ammon and Israel's need for a leader to fight against them
The psalmist uses the same expression about holding his life in his hand, meaning constant danger
A similar situation where Ephraim complained about not being called to battle, showing a pattern of internal conflict in Israel
